issues.text: release.yml does not run 'when a version is released': it runs when a version tag v*.*.* is pushed, and it is the workflow that then creates the GitHub release (release.yml:4 'Runs when a version tag such as v1.0.0 is pushed'; last step 'gh release create'). Cause and effect are reversed.
issues.quote: `release.yml`, the workflow that runs when a version is released,
issues.fix: Replace with: "`release.yml`, the workflow that runs when a version tag such as `v1.0.0` is pushed,".

issues.text: Non sequitur: that Git does not check the author name means the log's author column cannot be trusted to say who deployed; it is not why whoever can push decides what staging runs (that follows from automated sync, whatever name the commit carries).
issues.quote: Git does not check that name, so whoever can push to `envs/staging` decides what staging runs, and the repository needs the protection you would give the cluster.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Git does not check that name, so the column shows who a commit says it is from, not who pushed it. And whoever can push to `envs/staging` decides what staging runs, so the repository needs the protection you would give the cluster."

issues.text: The precondition is incomplete: gitops-first-sync.sh @ stage-3:3 says 'scripts/devops/argocd-install.sh and gitops-repo.sh come first'. A learner who has not run first-sync has most likely not run those either, and first-sync then fails.
issues.quote: If you have not run `scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.sh` in an earlier lesson, run it first.
issues.fix: Replace with: "If you have not run `scripts/devops/argocd-install.sh`, `scripts/devops/gitops-repo.sh` and `scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.sh` in earlier lessons, run them first, in that order."

issues.text: Line 22 runs `perl`, a program I have never seen named. The prose tells me what the line does (replaces the sha- tag with 1.0.0 in both files), so I can follow, but I do not know what perl is or why it, not a shell command I know, does the edit.
issues.fix: In 'Line 22 replaces the `sha-` tag with `1.0.0` in both files', add 'using perl, a text-editing program run from the shell,' after 'Line 22'.

issues.text: The excerpt uses `$from`, `$to` and `$config_repo`, which are set in lines 1–12, outside the block. I have to guess that $from is the current sha- tag, $to is 1.0.0 and $config_repo is a local copy of the config repository.
issues.quote: echo "== deploy $to: one commit to envs/staging"
issues.fix: Add one sentence before 'Line 22 replaces…': '`$from` and `$to`, set earlier in the script, hold the current `sha-` tag and `1.0.0`; `$config_repo` is a local clone of the config repository.'

issues.text: Line 11 of staging-auto.yaml points at `gitea.git.svc`. The word gitea appears nowhere in the prose; only later, in §4, does 'the Git server runs inside your donhang-staging cluster' let me guess that this is that server.
issues.fix: After 'Lines 3–16 match `staging-manual.yaml`', add: 'line 11 is the address of the Git server inside the cluster that holds the config repository.'

issues.text: The 'so' joins two ideas I could not link: Git not checking the author name tells me the log may lie about who deployed, but the reason whoever can push decides what staging runs is that a commit is the deploy. I re-read it to separate them.
issues.quote: Git does not check that name, so whoever can push to `envs/staging` decides what staging runs, and the repository needs the protection you would give the cluster.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: 'Git does not check that name, so the column says who a commit claims to be from. Since a commit is the deploy, whoever can push to `envs/staging` decides what staging runs, …'

issues.text: The lesson presents 'CI needs push rights, not cluster credentials' as the payoff and the situation's question asks how to avoid a command against the cluster, but no sentence says why cluster credentials in CI are worse than push rights to Git. I take it on trust.
issues.quote: CI needs the right to push to the config repository, not credentials for the cluster.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this one saying what is gained, tied to pull-based deployment: e.g. that the only thing able to change the cluster is the agent inside it, and every change it makes is a commit in `git log`.

issues.text: The third paragraph of §4 holds the reread interval, refresh vs sync, OutOfSync, the automated-sync trigger and the whole wave order. I had to read it twice to keep 'refresh' (compare only) apart from 'sync'.
issues.quote: Argo CD rereads the folder on its own at a regular interval, or at once when asked to refresh; a refresh only rereads Git and compares, it does not sync.
issues.fix: Start a new paragraph at 'With automated sync, a difference that comes from a new commit starts a sync', so detection and the sync it starts are two short paragraphs.

issues.text: Try it assumes the lab from earlier lessons exists. The text does not say what gitops-first-sync.sh needs or sets up, so if I skipped those lessons I would not know whether the donhang-staging cluster, Argo CD and the Git server must already be running.
issues.quote: If you have not run `scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.sh` in an earlier lesson, run it first.
issues.fix: In the same sentence, name the lesson(s) whose scripts must have run, so the reader knows which steps to go back to.

issues.text: q5 option d does not say whether deploy commits stop. I read it as 'keep commits, but sync by hand'; the explanation then says the sync 'finds nothing new', which confused me until its last sentence. I could still pick a, but the explanation made me doubt my reading.
issues.quote: But a push to `ghcr.io` changes nothing in Git, so such a sync finds nothing new, and asking for it is again a command against the cluster.
issues.fix: Make option d explicit, e.g. 'Remove the sync policy, keep the deploy commits, and have someone ask Argo CD for a sync after each one', and drop 'such a sync finds nothing new' from its explanation.
